doc.title: Anat Cohen interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 9, 2021

title: Finding 'one' in Latin rhythms through dancing
summary: Feeling comes before thinking; dancing helped with clave, and Jovino Santos Neto speaks of incorporating rhythm in the body.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: I’m remembering the thing you said about the Latin band in Boston and that you learned to move to the music and it gave me this flash like when I’ve tried to listen to Latin music sometimes I get aggravated, like I lose “one.” And I’m wondering if moving like that helps like keep one in your head.

You know that’s always, what you’re describing is always that conflict between the feeling and the thinking. Because what you feel is what you feel and nobody can argue with you. It’s always right, that’s what you feel. Now whether one person calls it “one” and another person calls it “four” that’s a whole other question and that’s when you want to write music or analyze music then maybe you need to know where is “one.” But the feeling is the feeling so there is first that. But it was not a natural thing for me to find “one” when there’s a clave and to be able to like [snaps fingers] to think and when the clave is moving and to talk about it and I was like okay where is the one, how do you know which one is the clave. Like it took me a while, and through dancing it definitely helped me stable that confidence. And you know my friend Jovino Santos Neto he is a great musician, he played for years with Hermeto Pascoal, a great educator and musician. He’s a piano player. And he talks about, you know, to incorporate a rhythm and the word “corpo” incorpo, the word “body” is in to incorporate. So you’ve got to move. You’ve got to dance, you’ve got to feel it with your body. And I think for me at different kinds of South American rhythms that I encountered, moving, dancing, stepping with the feet and first trusting the body movement, and then thinking about how it feels but going with the feeling first, it helped me understand a lot of music, and hanging out. Hang. Hanging out with the locals.
